ranked_facts.concept_key: Lesion fat-tissue attenuation with central contrast enhancement
ranked_facts.why: The lesion's fat-tissue attenuation with central contrast enhancement is more consistent with a lipoma than with a gastrointestinal stromal tumor or leiomyoma, which would not typically exhibit this characteristic appearance on imaging.

ranked_facts.concept_key: Submucosal bulging mass with ulcerated areas
ranked_facts.why: The presence of a submucosal bulging mass with ulcerated areas is more suggestive of a gastrointestinal stromal tumor or leiomyoma, which can cause mucosal ulceration, whereas a lipoma would be less likely to cause this finding.
